about: The Windows app-folder rule (R-31), as one table. Path tokens: `current` is <base>/<APP_AUTHOR>/<APP_NAME>, `legacy` is <base>/<LEGACY_APP_AUTHOR>/<APP_NAME>, `currentParent` and `legacyParent` are their author folders, `lookalike` is <base>/<LEGACY_APP_AUTHOR>2/<APP_NAME>, `marker` is the move marker's file name and `lock` is the move lock's. Each case builds `before` under an empty temporary base directory; a trailing slash makes an empty directory instead of a file. `unreadable` lists directories whose permissions are then removed, so checking a path below them fails (unix only, and skipped where the permissions are not enforced). `resolution` is run by both implementations, crates/biorouter-mcp/src/app_folder/tests.rs and ui/desktop/src/utils/appFolder.test.ts: it expects the folder named by `resolves`, with nothing moved. `moves` is run by the daemon's suite only, since only the daemon moves: it runs the move once per entry of `runs` (writing the marker, as for the roaming folder) and expects that outcome from each run, then the folder named by `resolves`, then every `exists` path present and every `absent` path missing. `renameFails` makes every rename attempt fail, as a file held open by another process does on Windows.

resolution.name: a fresh install resolves the current folder
the legacy folder alone stays in use until it is moved
the current folder alone is used
when both exist the current folder wins
a folder whose author only starts like the legacy one is not the legacy folder
a file where the legacy author folder would be is not a legacy folder
a legacy folder that cannot be checked may hold data, so it stays in use
a current folder that cannot be checked is still the current one when no legacy folder exists

moves.name: a fresh install starts in the current folder and creates nothing yet
the legacy folder alone is moved whole, marker inside, and its emptied author folder and lock removed
an author folder that also holds another app keeps it, and is not removed, but loses the lock
the current folder alone is used as it is
when both exist the current folder wins and the legacy one is left untouched
an empty legacy author folder, or one holding only the lock, that an interrupted run left behind is tidied
a folder whose author only starts like the legacy one is never touched
a refused rename keeps the legacy folder in use, with its marker for the next attempt
a refused rename never removes a current author folder it did not create
a legacy folder that cannot be checked is neither moved nor hidden by a new current folder
